newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NSE declares 5 brokers in default.
newsitem.headline: India's NSE declares 5 brokers in default.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) said on Tuesday it declared five brokers in default and suspended six other brokers for not honouring their commitments.
NSE managing director R.H. Patil told reporters the members had not complied with settlement dues. He did not immediately release details of the amounts involved.

The five brokers in default are: Maxwell Securities Pvt Ltd and R.C. Garg and Sons Capital Services Pvt Ltd, both of New Delhi, Ahmedabad-based Rahil Investments and Finance Ltd and Westfin Securities and Vipul Securities, both of Bombay.
It suspended Swaraj Financials & Investment Ltd, Opart Exports Pvt Ltd, Dalip Khosla Trading, Acquitor Trading & Investment, Praveira Financial Services and Capital Consortium Securities, Patil said.
The NSE is India's largest stock exchange and operates from 150 cities across the country.
